extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, installation commanders, A-76/competitive sourcing study teams, and acquisition staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons learned for planning, conducting, evaluating and administering A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies on military installations, including PWS, source selection, QASP, protests, and post-award actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve contracting officer early
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting officer should be involved very early in the study process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel are critical in supporting the PWS team by providing knowledge of contract requirements that must be represented in the PWS; early involvement can prevent later changes and errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include local union and keep employees informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Include local union and keep Government employees informed as to what is going on with the A-76 study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open communication policy is recommended, but communication should not divulge information that could prejudice the MEO or offerors or jeopardize integrity of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a sound Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sound Performance Work Statement is essential to the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must accurately reflect actual work; perform a Performance Requirements Review; avoid inflated PWSs that misrepresent work; third-party review/validation recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess manpower availability and capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and plan for manpower available to conduct studies; Government may be disadvantaged by inadequate in-house manpower resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training, use full‑time participants, consider bringing in retired civil servants; contractor supervisors are not the answer—leadership involvement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use competitive sourcing to motivate innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing can be used as effective motivation for Government and private industry to develop innovative ways of accomplishing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture innovation as a positive lesson learned and share successes across commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and analyze protests as lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether protests were lodged, describe nature and outcome to identify pitfalls to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use protest cases (Comptroller General decisions) to highlight requirements: follow published solicitation ground rules, ensure solicitations provide sufficient information for intelligent competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify lack of qualified gov personnel for QA as risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk includes not having Government personnel qualified to inspect contractor functions as Quality Assurance Evaluation members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of in‑house expertise over time makes it hard to survey contractor performance or re-write contracts after initial term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate worker reaction and workforce alienation
rubrics_metrics.description: Worker reaction—fear that PWS/MEO teams aim to take jobs—is a risk that can reduce support for teams and alienate workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate openly and manage expectations to reduce negative reactions and preserve in‑house expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate capture of workload data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to adequately capture workload data required by the organization is a key risk area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using previous studies as baseline; take a fresh look at current activities, inputs/outputs, and internal controls. Don't add tasks to stack the deck in favor of in‑house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find quality contractors who can meet performance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk in finding a quality contractor who can meet the Service's performance expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include desired performance factors and interfaces with management systems in Acquisition Strategy; require past performance matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid SOW/PWS that adds work to the MEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of Work or PWS must not add additional work by the MEO (if they win) beyond existing workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SOW/PWS aligns with actual workload figures to avoid change orders and cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for ability to meet timeline and transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Government's ability to meet published timeline and manage transition between Government and contractor/MEO is a recurrent risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop detailed milestones, tracking systems, and a single responsible individual to keep the study on schedule; phase-in plans should be solicitation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate potential protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential for protests is a risk to be managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cost comparisons and source selection follow announced ground rules in the solicitation; document decisions and bases to withstand protest review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for security clearances and IT manpower shortages
rubrics_metrics.description: Large number of positions and required security clearances (processing 12–24 months) and local IT manpower shortages can delay transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with manpower offices to retain sufficient staffing until clearances/training are complete; plan for hiring for the MEO as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider local labor market impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Local unemployment rates and local labor shortages for trades affect the ability to hire replacement personnel for MEO/contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor local labor availability into transition planning and timeline projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess mission impact and potential loss of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing may cause 'massive upheaval' to mission, loss of services, or loss of critical personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mission risk and plan mitigation to sustain mission during and after transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid loss of in-house expertise and customer focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of losing in-house expertise and alienation of the workforce, and losing focus on customer needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain mechanisms to preserve knowledge, involve functional personnel, and document procedures and lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage conflicts of interest and proprietary information exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of interest with Government employees and exposure to proprietary information during Management Plan development is a significant risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify forbidden personnel for the SSEB and other roles; develop lists of conflicts of interest and protect proprietary information appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and budget for cost of conducting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct cost of conducting commercial activity (A-76) studies is a risk—lack of funding may prevent studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess funding and resource requirements prior to initiating studies; consider timing and scope relative to available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware changing rules during ongoing studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing program rules affect current/ongoing studies and create risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance on handling rule changes and determine early planning decisions to mitigate impacts when rules change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question optimistic savings assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations such as an assumed 20% savings prior to study may be unrealistic and risk misaligned expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use realistic, evidence‑based savings projections and document assumptions; consider that expected savings may be unattainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study entire functions rather than parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should study an entire function (e.g., Public Works) instead of piecemeal studies to avoid perpetuating inefficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studying full function prevents later wasted effort and creates the most efficient organization for the entire function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and structure CA Team effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a Commercial Activities (CA) Team, subdivide into functional teams (PWS, MEO, IGCE, QASP), and consider an independent audit team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full-time participants, consider retired civil servants for expertise, and subdivide work so multiple tasks can proceed concurrently while the larger CA Team maintains coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Commercial Activity Executive Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Form an executive committee chaired by Installation Commander including directors, contracting officers, civilian personnel, and major commands to monitor the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee provides command oversight and decision-making; appoint a single individual to keep study moving to schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish installation guidance and letters of instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish installation regulations and letters of instruction to define responsibilities and duties of action officers and participating organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear local directives help ensure consistent roles and accountability throughout the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an Acquisition Strategy Panel early
rubrics_metrics.description: Form an Acquisition Strategy Panel to review contract type, use of incentives, disposition of Government property, desired performance factors, maintenance responsibilities, and required interfaces with automated systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide contract type early and gain concurrence to avoid rework; contract type decision should precede finalizing PWS and other contracting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop policy for unique labor sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide early how prisoners, volunteers, and borrowed military personnel will be treated in the PWS, MEO, and cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unique labor sources create challenges in workload accounting; formal policy prevents later disputes or inconsistent treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and require access to workload databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize database maintenance systems capable of updating the PWS when workload data change, and ensure Government access to contractor data on work performed and level of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data access requirements in the PWS and contract clauses to support oversight and avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Allowable Quality Levels (AQLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize most service contracts cannot be performed perfectly; solicitations should allow establishment of AQLs with reasonable levels of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AQLs should be realistic and used in evaluation and QASP to balance performance and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform Performance Requirements Review before proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Requirements Review should be accomplished prior to other portions of the A-76 study, especially the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures PWS reflects actual work; prevents developing MEO or contractor work scope that is inconsistent with real requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'getting well' via added requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't assume the commercial activity will gain additional manpower via adding work requirements; adding tasks to 'get well' is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If MEO wins and additional tasks were artificially added, staffing distortions and later problems may result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell bidders what to accomplish, not how
rubrics_metrics.description: PWS should describe required work, not prescribe how bidders must accomplish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific approaches are necessary, place them in Section L and include as evaluation criteria in the Source Selection Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PWS templates cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton or prior PWSs can be a jumping-off point but avoid copying old PWSs verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor templates to specific needs; templates speed completion but risk perpetuating outdated or inappropriate requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize proposal formats in Section L
rubrics_metrics.description: Section L should standardize formats to facilitate evaluation by the Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB) and specify contents of technical/cost proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require staffing charts linking positions to PWS functions and equate manning to proposed hours in the cost proposal; require past performance summary matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify SSEB members early and screen conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: SSEB members must be identified early to prevent tainting by prior participation; develop a list of personnel forbidden from serving due to conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early identification avoids schedule delays and protestable conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish source selection criteria and include price realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate and publish source selection criteria to guide decisions; Section M should state that price realism will be considered in addition to lowest price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear criteria reduce ambiguity and support defensible award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require phase-in and Contract Administration Plan (CAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in plans should be a solicitation requirement and evaluated; develop a CAP that includes QASP inspections and contract administration duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stagger changeover over months, set final date for contractor full responsibility, and use CAP to ensure QASP inspection compliance and use functional expertise in administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administer QASP to protect contractor and Government
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP must ensure contractor meets AQLs and that inspectors do not impose requirements beyond the contract scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional personnel should select surveillance methods; contracting officer must correct improper inspector requirements to avoid Board of Contract Appeals findings of liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle differing site conditions cooperatively
rubrics_metrics.description: When site conditions differ from contract assumptions, Government and contractor should mutually agree actions to avoid material breach and start relationships properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve differences early and document agreements to maintain good relations and avoid appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and disseminate lessons learned in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government employees and contractors supporting the A-76 study should capture lessons learned in writing and make them available to other commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO recommended a comprehensive lessons learned system due to limited DoD resources devoted to documenting best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation must provide sufficient information for intelligent competition
rubrics_metrics.description: A procuring agency must provide prospective bidders with information sufficient to enable bidders to compete intelligently and on a relatively equal basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IFB need not eliminate all uncertainties; however, ambiguous specifications left unaddressed can force offerors to assume undue risk and create protest grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow announced ground rules for cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must be conducted in accordance with criteria established within the solicitation (announced 'ground rules').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO/Comptroller General reviews focus on whether the agency followed its announced ground rules; deviations can be the basis for sustaining protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define evaluation factors and consequences for unacceptable subfactors
rubrics_metrics.description: State evaluation areas (technical plan, organization and management plan, quality control, past performance, transition plan) and indicate that any factor or sub‑factor judged unacceptable will render the entire area unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define unacceptable thresholds and ensure offerors understand the risk of receiving an unacceptable rating in an area.
